episode_title: From Photographer to AI Founder: Steve Moraco on Building DATA
question: What happened to Lander Media and Data when it reached 2000 subscribers and 40000 people on the waitlist?
transcript_excerpt: The platform experienced severe technical issues and churn reached 30% per month, making it clear the system was not sustainable. Steve made five seats available and they sold out in 24 hours, forcing him to pause new sales and return to the drawing board to redesign the offering.

episode_title: From Photographer to AI Founder: Steve Moraco on Building DATA
question: Why did Steve Moraco choose to study art at SCAD instead of pursuing computer science?
transcript_excerpt: After shadowing his father at HP in 2008 during mass layoffs, he saw many sad people in cubicles and decided against a tech career. He preferred the idea of being outside taking pictures and getting a degree while doing photography rather than homework, which excited him much more.

episode_title: From Photographer to AI Founder: Steve Moraco on Building DATA
question: How did Steve Moraco discover he had a talent for event photography?
transcript_excerpt: He volunteered as a photographer for First Lego League, a tech competition where high schoolers compete with Lego robots, for years during high school after his father introduced him to it. He discovered he loved figuring out when cool moments were about to happen and being ready to capture them, a skill he still uses today.

episode_title: From Photographer to AI Founder: Steve Moraco on Building DATA
question: What was Steve Moraco's first business venture after college?
transcript_excerpt: His first business was a book designed to help people get scholarships to study abroad. He was so enamored with his own study abroad experiences that he wanted to help more students access those opportunities while in college, though this venture ultimately failed.

episode_title: From Photographer to AI Founder: Steve Moraco on Building DATA
question: How did Steve Moraco manage to study abroad in Hong Kong during his final semester when initially told it was impossible?
transcript_excerpt: He persisted in asking open-ended questions about how to meet university requirements while still doing his semester abroad. The university eventually allowed him to walk across the stage a year early with his freshman-year cohort, and then he completed his study abroad semester in Hong Kong after graduation.
